memory_update.text: For leading-edge foundry and semiconductor equipment, keep TSM and ASML as anchor names because they map directly to wafer capacity and EUV lithography scarcity.
Add AMAT, LRCX and KLAC as core US-listed WFE/process-control candidates tied to AI-driven leading-edge logic, DRAM/HBM and advanced packaging investment.

Potential second-order suppliers not included due to the 5-candidate cap: TER for AI/HBM test, FORM for probe cards and test subsystems, MKSI for vacuum/photonics/laser/precision subsystems, AEIS for power subsystems, and ENTG for specialty materials/filtration. These should be checked in a follow-up supplier-components pass.

Current evidence suggests the node is real but may bifurcate: near-term AI scarcity appears concentrated in advanced packaging/HBM, while WFE/lithography/process-control governs the medium-term rate of supply expansion.

node: Leading-edge foundry capacity and semiconductor equipment
summary: Expanded the node universe toward US-listed foundry and semiconductor-capital-equipment exposures most directly tied to AI accelerator supply expansion. The highest-relevance names are TSMC for leading-edge foundry and advanced packaging capacity; ASML for EUV lithography scarcity; Applied Materials for deposition, materials engineering and advanced packaging tools; Lam Research for etch/deposition/process steps tied to GAA, memory and packaging; and KLA for inspection/metrology/process control intensity. These are research candidates only, not recommendations.
